is

proximal dilatation may be secondary to mass effect from the

3.  Large infrarenal aortic aneurysm is unchanged but better

4.  Air within the endometrial cavity, unchanged and of

Endoscopy ___

Procedure: The procedure, indications, preparation and potential 
complications were explained to the patient, who indicated her 
understanding and signed the corresponding consent forms.

A 
physical exam was performed.

The patient was administered 
moderate sedation.

The physical exam was performed prior to 
administering anesthesia.
Supplemental oxygen was used.

The 
patient was placed in the left lateral decubitus position.The 
digital exam was normal.

The colonoscope was introduced through 
the rectum and advanced under direct visualization until the
Proximal Rectum was reached.

The colonoscope was retroflexed 
within the rectum.

Careful visualization was performed as the 
instrument was withdrawn.
The procedure was not difficult.

The 
quality of the preparation was poor.
Visualization of the
Proximal Rectum and sigmoid colon was poor.

The patient 
tolerated the procedure well.
There were no complications.
Findings:

Contents: Solid stool was noted in the rectum limiting complete 
mucosal evaluation.

Other There was a ridge of abnormal mucosa at what is likely 
the anastomotic site from prior colorectal surgery.

There was 
some evidence of oozing from this area, but complete evaluation 
was limited based on presence of solid stool.

Appearance was 
somewhat concerning for recurrence, and was thought to most 
likely be the bleeding source, although a more proximal source 
of bleeding could not definitively be excluded.

Cold forceps 
biopsies were performed for histology at the rectum.

Endoscopy ___
Findings: Esophagus:

Mucosa: Localized erythema of the mucosa with no bleeding was 
noted in the gastroesophageal junction.

These findings are 
compatible with esophagitis.
Stomach:
Lumen: A small size hiatal hernia was seen.

Mucosa: Patchy erythema of the mucosa with no bleeding was 
noted in the antrum.

These findings are compatible with 
gastritis.

Cold forceps biopsies were performed for histology at 
the stomach antrum.
Duodenum:
Mucosa: Normal mucosa was noted in the whole duodenum.

Cold 
forceps biopsies were performed for histology at the duodenal 
bulb and second part of the duodenum.

Impression: Erythema in the gastroesophageal junction compatible 
with esophagitis
Small hiatal hernia
Erythema in the antrum compatible with gastritis (biopsy)
Normal mucosa in the whole duodenum (biopsy)
Otherwise normal EGD to third part of the duodenum
Reasonable to continue low dose daily PPI.

Proceed 
with colonoscopy for evaluation of bleeding source.
Gastrointestinal mucosal biopsies:
1.  Antrum (A):
Antral mucosa with chronic, focally active gastritis.
H. pylori immuno Stain will be reported in an addendum.
2.  Duodenum (B):

Duodenal mucosa, no diagnostic abnormalities recognized; see 
note.

Note: There is a separate fragment of foveolar 
epithelium, which likely represents a carry-over from part 1 and 
probably not a feature of chronic duodenitis.
3.  Rectum (C):

Colonic mucosa with focal areas of granulation tissue and ulcer, 
no carcinoma seen.
Additional levels will be reported in an addendum.
ADDENDUM:
Immunostain for H. pylori performed on part 1 (A) is negative.

Additional levels on part 3 (C) have been examined and show no 
carcinoma.
